description:
Owner's decision, 2026-11-08: yes (Lectern page muster-ui-redesign, decision 3).

Messages lists one row for every agent the person has messaged, each named @human+<callsign>: nine in his window on 2026-11-08, with one unread. When that agent has a pane, its row in the agent list carries the conversation instead, as an envelope with the unread count that opens it. Messages keeps conversations with several members and agents whose pane is gone, so his nine rows become two.

Cost: a one-to-one conversation with nothing unread is reached from the agent's row rather than from Messages.

Fencil decision one-to-one-on-agent-row (owner-decided).

## Plan (reviewed 2026-11-08)

From the plan for the redesign, step 4; the parent card a_2wKW8eBfM has its overall shape, order and checks.

A group's name cannot say who is in it. Pair groups are named from callsigns, which outlive their
panes and are reused by later ones, get `-2` and `-3` suffixes on collision (`pair_name` in
`crates/muster-msg/src/service.rs`), and keep their name when members join or leave
(`group_members`). A participant's name is not always its pane's id either: `join --name` and
`adopt` keep an explicit name. And the human's home daemon does not hold a remote member's pane.

What does know is the request the open conversation's member column already makes:
`session::conversation::refresh_members` asks the group's daemon `Who` as the human, outside the
session lock, and the daemon merges each remote member's answer from its own machine. Each member
comes back with its pane, which `pane_of` finds across the attached machines. The partner comes from
that, and the daemon protocol does not change.

- The core keeps a partner for each group the human is in: when `Who` lists exactly two members and
  one is the human, the other member's name and the pane id it reported; otherwise none.
- It asks `Who` for a group, off the session lock as `refresh_members` does, when the group first
  appears among the human's notices, when its notice changes, when an attached daemon connects or
  reconnects, and when any attached machine's set of panes changes.
- **Open, settled by a spike before this step is built.** Two changes reach none of those
  triggers: a member joining or leaving a pair the human has read to zero unread, without a post,
  and a partner adopted into a pane that already exists, locally or on another machine. Today the
  daemon tells the windows of a membership change only when the human leaves, and both the daemon
  (`tell_human`) and the core's mirror drop a notice identical to the last. So the daemon needs an
  observable signal for membership and pane-binding changes in the human's groups, such as a
  revision on the human's notices that the group's keeper bumps; how a remote member's binding
  change reaches it is the open part. The spike chooses the mechanism and passes this test, run
  against the real daemon with no synthesized notices: create every pane before the first lookup,
  read the pair to zero unread, add and then remove a third member, and move the named partner
  between two existing panes, with no posts and no reconnects; after each, `GroupsChanged` and the
  row placement are right. The test runs for a partner on the human's machine and for one on
  another machine. If the mechanism changes the daemon protocol, it takes the next protocol minor,
  and its concrete wire design is reviewed before it becomes the production contract.
- Everything that depends on knowing the partner waits for the spike: the envelope on the row,
  leaving the group out of Messages, and naming a one-to-one banner after the agent.
- It resolves the reported pane id to a `PaneKey` with `pane_of` each time it asks and again
  whenever a machine's panes change, so a notice that arrives before the remote pane's snapshot
  resolves once the snapshot lands.
- A failed `Who` keeps the last partner known, and logs at info as `refresh_members` does.
- `MessageGroup` in `GroupsChanged` gains `partner_pane`, set from that map. The partner is kept
  apart from the notice, so a notice that falls to zero unread does not clear it. `announce_groups`
  runs when a partner changes as well as on `HumanNoticed`, and `groups_sent` compares whole entries,
  `partner_pane` included.
- `partner_pane` is the same in every window, because it comes from the group's membership rather
  than any window's layout. Each window decides where to draw it: a group whose `partner_pane` is a
  row in that window's roster is drawn as an envelope badge on that row and left out of that
  window's Messages; in any other window, or once the pane closes, it stays in Messages. Moving the
  agent's tab between windows moves the badge with the roster.
- A click on the badge opens the conversation, as clicking the Messages row does today.
- Tests: a pair with a pane; a pair whose agent's pane closed; a third member joining; a group kept
  on the human's machine with an explicitly named remote member; a group kept on another machine
  and replicated to the human's; a named participant moving to a new pane without a post; a notice
  that arrives before the remote pane's snapshot; reading the pair to zero unread; two machines whose
  agents share a callsign; a callsign reused by a new pane; two windows, with the agent's tab moved
  from one to the other while the unread count is unchanged.
title: A one-to-one conversation with an agent that has a pane shows on that agent's row
